bullets.text: He believes his level is trending up and he's positioned for a strong second half if he plays to his standard.
bullets.quote: if I play the level that I know I, I guess, or I think I should be playing for the rest of the year... I'm in a decent place to still have a strong finish

bullets.text: Fritz emphasizes his strong ability to stay present and move past mistakes on court.
bullets.quote: I don't really let things bother me, especially when I'm on the court. I try to stay very in the moment.

bullets.text: He feels the extended schedule has made the season notably longer and more taxing.
bullets.quote: it feels like I'm playing more matches. It feels like the season got longer to me... now that we're doing it, yeah, it feels, like, really long.

bullets.text: Fritz is frustrated by inconsistent ball quality, saying practice balls can differ greatly from tournament balls.
bullets.quote: what's the point of practicing if the ball that I'm practicing with is going to be completely different to the one here?

bullets.text: Shelton felt he had to raise his level and rates his return games as central, having broken a big server three times.
bullets.quote: those return games are really key for me in my success

bullets.text: He views D.C.'s courts as favorable and wants to be sharp on this surface heading to the US Open.
bullets.quote: this is a good surface for me, and it's a surface that I want to be sharp when I get to New York

bullets.text: Notes the courts reward aggressive serving when hot and fast, though the rain delay dampened conditions today.
bullets.quote: when it's hot outside and the ball is moving fast and bouncing, which we had a little bit less of today

bullets.text: Used the extended break to grind on his body and fitness rather than rest.
bullets.quote: there was a lot of work for me to put in in terms of my body, my fitness

bullets.text: Sees the come-from-behind win as a confidence builder to start the swing after a disappointing Wimbledon.
bullets.quote: These are the type of matches that kind of propel you to playing really good tennis

bullets.text: Atmane broke through mentally by convincing himself he could finally beat Tiafoe after three straight losses.
bullets.quote: just trying to truly believe that I could get it, that I could get this win

bullets.text: Admits it took him a full set to reach peak level after a long layoff from hard courts.
bullets.quote: First match on hard court after, like, four month, you know, so it's never easy to come back at the peak, peak level

bullets.text: Found the humid night-session conditions difficult, with poor ball visibility.
bullets.quote: it's very humid. We can't see really well the ball on these kind of night sessions

bullets.text: Both players lacked rhythm having just transitioned from the grass season.
bullets.quote: Here we had zero rhythm, both of us. We came from grass, so it's not easy also to adapt
